STOP. The current implementation is invalid and must be discarded.


You are not allowed to create placeholder code, console fallbacks, simulated AI creation steps, fake neural pathway initialization, or methods containing pass for required functionality.


The source of truth is the existing Lyra 0.0.1 requirements and architecture documentation in this repository. Implement the actual application, not a demonstration.


Before writing code:


Read every relevant requirement and architecture document completely.
Identify the actual required application boundaries: GUI, onboarding, Brain, identity, personality, memory, model abstraction and persistence.
Do not invent requirements or behavior not documented.


The onboarding must be a real functional GUI application for Linux. It must use the actual architecture instead of embedding the entire onboarding logic in one procedural class.


Do not implement a console fallback.
Do not use fake progress messages.
Do not use pass for required functionality.
Do not claim functionality is implemented until it is actually executable.


After implementation:


run the application;
exercise the complete GUI onboarding flow;
verify every screen and interaction;
inspect runtime errors;
fix all errors;
run it again;
only then report completion.


If the requirements are architecturally incomplete, inspect the repository documentation and make the smallest implementation necessary to preserve the documented architecture. Do not replace the architecture with a toy prototype.
